paper.title_en: No complete set of mutually unbiased bases in C^6 without Fourier vanishing
paper.abstract_en: A recent exact certificate shows that C^6 admits no seven mutually unbiased bases, hence at most five (OpenAI, 2026). That argument has two parts. The first proves the Fourier-vanishing conjecture of Matolcsi, Ruzsa and Weiner for every complex Hadamard matrix of order six other than Tao's cubic matrix, and excludes the cubic matrix separately. The second feeds this vanishing into a positivity certificate on mixed moments of a hypothetical complete family. We show that the first part is not needed. We keep the same six families of test functions and the same linear identities, but we never set a moment to zero because of Fourier vanishing. New positive definite integer matrices still give the contradiction. The only inputs are orthonormality, unbiasedness, the second-moment (2-design) identity of a complete family, and the trivial bound |moment| <= 1. A standard-library program checks the certificate in exact integer and rational arithmetic in under a minute and a half. We also record computational observations that are not part of the proof: a systematic S_6-symmetric family of test functions appears to close the argument with relations of total order at most 7 instead of 11, and at order 9 two orbit types of test charges appear to suffice. In the prime-power dimensions 4,5,7,8, where complete families exist, the same pipeline finds no certificate, as it must.
